indication.text: TIVDAK is indicated for the treatment of adult patients with recurrent or metastatic cervical cancer with disease progression on or after chemotherapy (accelerated approval).

citations.quote: TIVDAK™ is indicated for the treatment of adult patients with recurrent or metastatic cervical cancer with disease progression on or after chemotherapy.

This indication is approved under accelerated approval based on tumor response rate and durability of response [see *Clinical Studies* (14.1)]. Continued approval for this indication may be contingent upon verification and description of clinical benefit in confirmatory trials.

target_moa.text: Tisotumab vedotin is a tissue factor (TF)-directed antibody-drug conjugate: a human anti-TF IgG1 kappa antibody linked via a protease-cleavable valine-citrulline linker to the microtubule-disrupting agent monomethyl auristatin E (MMAE), which induces cell cycle arrest and apoptosis.

citations.quote: Tisotumab vedotin-tftv is a tissue factor (TF)-directed antibody drug conjugate (ADC). It contains a human anti-TF IgG1 kappa antibody, a protease-cleavable valine-citrulline linker, and a monomethyl auristatin E (MMAE) payload which is a microtubule-disrupting agent.

Tisotumab vedotin is an antibody drug conjugate (ADC) consisting of a human tissue factor (TF)-specific monoclonal antibody linked to monomethyl auristatin E (MMAE), an anti-microtubule small molecule that induces cell cycle arrest and apoptosis, via a protease-cleavable valine-citrulline (vc) linker.
Tisotumab vedotin-tftv is a tissue factor (TF)-directed antibody drug conjugate (ADC).

key_safety.text: Fatal adverse reactions occurred in 4% (septic shock, pneumonitis); serious adverse reactions in 43% (ileus 6%, hemorrhage 5%, pneumonia 4%). Most common adverse reactions (≥30%) included fatigue, nausea, peripheral neuropathy, alopecia, epistaxis, conjunctival adverse reactions, and hemorrhage. Ocular toxicity affected 55% of patients, including 6% with ulcerative keratitis.

citations.quote: Fatal adverse reactions occurred in 4% of patients and included septic shock and pneumonitis. Serious adverse reactions occurred in 43% of patients and included ileus (6%), hemorrhage (5%), pneumonia (4%), sepsis (3%), constipation (3%), pyrexia (3%), and peripheral neuropathy (3%). The most common adverse reactions (\ge30%) in GCT1015-04 included fatigue, nausea, peripheral neuropathy, alopecia, epistaxis, conjunctival adverse reactions, and hemorrhage.

Ocular toxicity is an important safety signal associated with tisotumab vedotin and affected 55% of patients enrolled to GCT1015-04, including 6% of patients with ulcerative keratitis, including one patient with a corneal ulcer that perforated and required corneal transplantation.

detail.text: Boxed Warning for ocular toxicity: TIVDAK caused changes in the corneal epithelium and conjunctiva resulting in changes in vision, including severe vision loss, and corneal ulceration.

citations.quote: ## WARNING: OCULAR TOXICITY
- TIVDAK caused changes in the corneal epithelium and conjunctiva resulting in changes in vision, including severe vision loss, and corneal ulceration. [see *Warnings and Precautions* (5.1)].

detail.text: No companion diagnostic is required; the indication is regardless of tumor TF status and TF expression was not required for enrollment.

citations.quote: The Applicant seeks an indication in patients with recurrent or metastatic cervical cancer, regardless of tumor TF status. FDA agrees with this indication, and there is no need for a companion diagnostic to support this indication.
Based on the data available, a companion diagnostic is not needed to select patients for treatment with tisotumab vedotin.
